thread:
Morgan: Customer AcmeApp (acct: acme-prod) reports repeated failures in prod when invoking the `place_order` tool in JSON mode after last night's model rollout. Error visible in logs: `invalid_function_call: missing required property 'order_ids'`. Repro steps and payload below.

Morgan: Request we received (from customer's side):
```json
{
  "tool": "place_order",
  "args": "{\"orderIds\":[\"123\"],\"user_id\":\"u-9\"}"
}
```

Morgan: Runtime response:
```json
{
  "error": "invalid_function_call",
  "details": "required property order_ids missing",
  "model": "open-llm-v2-rc"
}
```

Priya: :eyes: That looks like `args` is a string (double-encoded). Also the key is `orderIds` (camelCase) while the schema expects `order_ids` (snake_case). Any chance the customer changed their SDK call or the model changed function argument casing?

Morgan: Customer says they didn't change client code. They were on SDK v1.9.2 but only started failing after our model update ~02:10 UTC. They attached a minimal repro snippet they used locally.

Carlos: I pulled our ingress logs for AcmeApp. Confirmed runtime received `args` as a string containing escaped JSON. Example: `args="{\"orderIds\":[\"123\"]}\"`. Two issues: (1) double-encoded args (string instead of object) and (2) function arg name drift (model or extractor emitted `orderIds` instead of `order_ids`). Older model variant tolerated camelCase via our loose coercion; new model enforces the declared function schema more strictly.

Sasha: On the model side, the v2 RC included a small change in the function serialization layer (normalizes some names for human-readability). That may have flipped the casing. I'm verifying which release introduced it.

DevBot: Created ticket INF-3721 (runtime + model) and added labels: customer-impact, hotfix. https://redwood.atlassian/INF-3721

Priya: Customer is asking for a fast workaround. Can we do a runtime lenient parse: if `args` is a string, attempt `JSON.parse`, and if parsed keys don't match required schema, try camelCase -> snake_case mapping for known fields (`orderIds` -> `order_ids`, etc.)? Also they are getting heavy retry traffic causing billing surge.

Carlos: I can ship a conservative hotfix to runtime that: (A) if `args` is type string, run safe JSON.parse + schema validation; (B) try a little key normalization map for backward compatibility. Will add a debug flag and only enable for requests arriving from known affected customers to limit risk. Spinning up a canary build now.

Morgan: ETA for canary? Customer wants status and we should also freeze retries on client side if possible.

Carlos: Canary build deployed to 3 nodes in us-west-2 in 10m. Early results: out of 120 failing calls, 108 now decode and validate. Logs show we correctly parsed stringified args and mapped `orderIds` -> `order_ids`.

Sophie: Billing saw ~430 extra token charges from retries over the last 2 hours for AcmeApp. I'll open a credit request and hold off on automatic charges while we confirm fix.

Priya: Noted, I'll update the customer (they asked for a credit & confirmation once prod is healthy).

Carlos: Promoting hotfix to prod in 30m after additional smoke tests. Patch: runtime v1.43.1 with safe-parse + key-normalization. Rollout plan posted in INF-3721.

Morgan: Thanks. Once prod is done please paste a small sample sanitized request/response so I can validate with the customer. Also capture the root cause summary for postmortem: (1) model function serialization changed casing; (2) some clients still stringified `args` — prior runtime tolerated both but new stricter path collided with string input -> schema validate failed.

Sasha: Will add model note. We should add a test in the model CI to check function argument casing stability.

DevBot: INF-3721 updated: hotfix deployed to canary, billing notified, postmortem scheduled.

Support-Bot: Closing loop with customer requested. Will reopen if more failures observed.

Priya: Customer acknowledged workaround and will monitor for 24h. Closing the support escalation once prod rollout completes. :white_check_mark:
